verdict.rationale: Ramp documents OAuth 2.0 with granular `resource:permission` scopes and explicit least-privilege guidance ("configure only the scopes your app needs"), plus Client Credentials for server-to-server use. Agent-specific identity is covered by "one key per agent" tied to a human sponsor with per-agent permissions, and headless `ramp agent login` exchanges client credentials for a token. A live probe confirms the MCP server publishes a long list of granular read/write scopes, and admins can restrict MCP access by role, department or user. Missing for 10: no hands-on or independent verification of actually issuing a narrowly scoped agent credential and having out-of-scope calls rejected.
